thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran a replay-harness job against last week's prod traces and hit some non-deterministic diffs after a kernel swap. Not sure if it's anonymization / sampling or an actual runtime regression.

sam: Ugh. Which kernel and config?

maya: Swapped from `kernel-v2.1` -> `kernel-v3.0-quant` on the same model build. Config: `--batching=continuous --kv-eviction=lru --warmup-prefix=200`. Command I used:
```
./replay-run --trace=prod-2026-03-10.tgz --model=redwood/open-11b:v7 --kernel=kernel-v3.0-quant --anonymize=cohort --sample-rate=0.02 --compare-to=kernel-v2.1 --metrics=token_match,p95_latency
```

kai: Were you using the same quantization profile and no-kernel-fallback flags? `v3.0-quant` changes matmul kernels and the numeric reduction order sometimes.

maya: Yes same qprofile file (qprof-2026-02-20.json). I set `--force-quant-profile` and `--disable-mixed-kernel-fallback`.

replay-bot: Anonymization applied: user_id -> cohort_XX, prompt hashes stored. Sampling: deterministic seed=42 applied.

henry: Can you paste the parity summary? even a tiny table.

maya: Pasted short JSON metrics snippet below:
```json
{
  "token_match_rate_overall": "98.3%",
  "token_match_rate_seq_gt_1024": "74.1%",
  "p95_latency_kernel_v2.1": "124ms",
  "p95_latency_kernel_v3.0-quant": "118ms",
  "kv_warmup_hit_after_prefix": "0.56",
  "samples_analyzed": "6,214"
}
```

nora: So latency improved but token match collapsed on long sequences. That smells like KV cache difference: either cache population order or eviction policy. `--warmup-prefix=200` might be insufficient for sequences >1024.

sam: Could also be numerical nondet from different matmul reductions on quant kernel. But 74% drop only for long sequences points to state divergence, not tiny float diffs. Float noise usually still correlates.

kai: Agreed. Two hypotheses: (1) KV eviction differences (LIFO vs LRU edge case) when prefix length is low and sequence length spikes; (2) batching heuristic change in v3 that reorders micro-batches causing KV alignment mismatch.

henry: How deterministic was the replay harness run? Was tracing deterministic with respect to request ordering?

maya: We used the deterministic replay mode (replay-bot stamped seed=42) and pinned worker affinity. But we had autoscaling disabled only for the run — not the per-request route-mirroring.

replay-bot: Note: trace contains ~3% of sessions with abrupt session-resume events (client reconnect) — these are anonymized but still present as separate trace lines.

nora: Those reconnects can cause duplicate prefix insertions in KV cache if the replay pipeline doesn't coalesce session ids after anonymization. That would explain the warmup_hit metric at 0.56.

sam: Action plan proposed:
- reproduce minimal failing sample set (start with 200 sequences >1024)
- run three controlled configs: `v2.1`, `v3.0-quant` w/ current flags, `v3.0-quant` with `--kv-eviction=none` and `--batching=flush-each`
- add a trace preprocessor pass to coalesce anonymized session ids and collapse reconnects for apples-to-apples KV behavior
- instrument the runtime to emit `kv.put` / `kv.get` ops with logical sequence id tags (sampling only)

kai: I'll own the `--kv-eviction=none` run + microtrace instrumentation. Will add a small probe that logs first 512 KV keys per session (sampled).

henry: I'll run the reprocessor to coalesce reconnects and produce a 'coalesced' trace slice. I'll also add a flag `--preserve-session-boundaries` to the harness for comparison.

maya: I'll pick a 200-sample long-seq cohort and run the three configs. I'll also generate token-level diff dumps for the first divergence index.

replay-bot: Job queued: `replay/2198765432/kv-warmup-investigation` — expect ~2h.

nora: When we do apples-to-apples, ensure kernel ABI, quant profile, and CPU host lib versions match exactly. Add an env dump to each run: `LD_PRELOAD`, `CUDA/ROCm` driver versions, and `libc` if relevant.

sam: Also add a tiny eval: feed divergent prefixes into a cold isolate to see if same divergence reproduces from scratch (isolates away batch ordering effects).

maya: Good idea. I'll do the cold isolate runs under `--batching=single` so we remove micro-batch reorder.

henry: If this reproduces, it's almost certainly a kernel numeric diff. If not, likely KV or batching order.

nora: FYI: we should keep anonymization consistent, but add a mapping table for the sampled session ids so we can cross-check session coalescing while still preserving privacy.

maya: Cool. I'll post results in this thread once runs finish. Preliminary triage: priority=high (affects rollout of v3.0-quant), owner=@maya, expected follow-up Monday. :eyes:

sam: thx. ping @eng-runtime on major regression if token_match_rate_seq_gt_1024 < 80% on full sample.

kai: Adding small note: capture kernel symbol version too (`nm -D libkernel.so | head`) so we can diff approved kernels.

maya: will do. /cc replay-bot for logs.

replay-bot: Run complete: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-replay/artifacts/2198765432/ — includes `parity-diffs.tar.gz`, `kv-microtraces/`, and `env-dumps/`.

maya: Uploaded initial parity-diffs, pushing the 200-long-sample runs now.

henry: Thanks — will review and post a short postmortem note if we confirm root cause.

nora: great, let's avoid rolling v3.0-quant to Dedicated until we have an apples-to-apples green. :+1:
